issues.t: Clutch slipping or wearing out early
issues.sym: The engine revs climb but the car doesn't speed up to match, especially in higher gears or on hills. Some owners notice grinding, shudder, a burning smell or a clutch that suddenly stops working.
issues.why: Clutch and flywheel wear is the most-reported problem on the second-generation Tiburon, with many manual-transmission cars needing a clutch well before 50,000 miles. Some cars needed more than one clutch.
issues.next: Have the clutch checked as soon as it slips; slipping gets worse quickly and can damage the flywheel. Ask for a clutch kit and flywheel inspection or replacement at the same time.

issues.t: Clutch pedal sticks or won't go into gear from a hydraulic leak
issues.sym: The clutch pedal feels soft, sinks to the floor, or sticks down, and the car grinds or refuses to go into gear.
issues.why: The clutch master or slave cylinder leaks internally or externally, so the clutch no longer fully releases.
issues.next: Check the clutch fluid reservoir (it shares fluid with the brakes on many cars) and look for wetness near the pedal or transmission. Replace the leaking cylinder and bleed the system.

issues.t: Timing belt due or broken
issues.sym: Usually no warning. A worn belt may squeal or tick; if it breaks, the engine stalls and won't restart.
issues.why: Every Tiburon engine uses a rubber timing belt with a set replacement interval. When it breaks, the engine stops and can suffer valve damage.
issues.next: If there's no record of a belt change in the last 60,000 to 100,000 miles, have it done now, along with the tensioner and water pump. Don't keep driving if you suspect the belt is failing.

issues.t: Airbag warning light stays on
issues.sym: The airbag (SRS) light stays lit or comes and goes, sometimes with a seat belt chime.
issues.why: Damaged wiring at the seat belt buckle under the seat, a faulty buckle sensor, or a failed airbag control module are common causes reported by owners.
issues.next: Have the SRS codes read. Airbags may not work properly while the light is on, so get it fixed rather than just reset.

issues.t: Seat belt buckle wiring can stop the airbag from working (recall)
issues.sym: The airbag light may be on, or there may be no warning at all.
issues.why: The driver seat height adjuster can pinch and damage the seat belt buckle wiring, which can keep the airbag from deploying in a crash.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls and have a dealer inspect and repair the wiring free of charge.

issues.t: Passenger airbag may not open properly (recall)
issues.sym: No symptoms. You may have received a recall letter about the passenger airbag.
issues.why: The instrument panel on some 2003 cars was not torn in the right pattern for the passenger airbag to deploy as designed.
issues.next: Confirm with a dealer that the recall was done.

issues.t: Rear brake lines can rub through and leak (recall)
issues.sym: A soft or sinking brake pedal, a brake warning light, or brake fluid on the ground.
issues.why: Rear brake tubes could contact steering gearbox brackets and wear through, leaking brake fluid and reducing braking.
issues.next: If the brake pedal sinks, feels soft or goes closer to the floor, or a red brake warning comes on, slow down gently, use a lower gear, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on: call for a tow. If the pedal is soft, stop driving. Have a dealer check the VIN and reroute or replace the lines under the recall.

issues.t: Fuel tank valve may leak fuel in a rollover (recall)
issues.sym: No symptoms in normal driving.
issues.why: A valve in the fuel tank may not close completely, so fuel could spill in a rollover crash and start a fire.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to confirm the fuel tank valve recalls were completed.

issues.t: Front lower control arms rust through (recall)
issues.sym: Clunks from the front end, a wheel that tilts or shifts, or the car hopping when braking.
issues.why: In road-salt states the front lower control arms can corrode and crack. Owners report failures even after the recall inspection.
issues.next: Have the control arms inspected for rust and the recall checked. Replace any arm that shows perforation.

issues.t: Steering inner ball joints may crack (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking or looseness in the steering. In the worst case, a front wheel can lose steering control.
issues.why: Some 2005 Tiburons were built with inner tie rod ball joints that may have internal cracks.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall and have it done right away if it is open.

issues.t: Brake lights fail from a faulty switch (recall)
issues.sym: Brake lights stay on, or do not come on when you press the pedal.
issues.why: The brake light switch can malfunction. Hyundai recalled about 1.7 million vehicles including the Tiburon to replace it.
issues.next: Have someone watch the brake lights while you press the pedal. Ask a dealer to check for the open recall.

issues.t: Turn signals or hazards stuck on from a failed body control module
issues.sym: Turn signals or hazard lights stay on, won't cancel or stop working. Sunroof, headlight or door lock problems can show up at the same time.
issues.why: A relay inside the body control module fails, according to many owner reports.
issues.next: Have the electrical system diagnosed. A replacement body control module, programmed to the car, is the usual fix.

issues.t: Melted climate control switch or wiring
issues.sym: A burning plastic smell, smoke from the dash, or the fan and climate controls stop working.
issues.why: Owners report melted climate-control switches, connectors and harness wiring, sometimes more than once.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and leave the hood closed. Call 911 from a safe spot, even if you can't see flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Stop using the fan and have the wiring inspected right away if you smell burning. Replace damaged connectors, not just the switch.

issues.t: Gas pump clicks off early or fuel smell after filling
issues.sym: The pump keeps shutting off after a gallon or so, filling takes a long time, fuel overflows, or there's a gas smell and a check engine light.
issues.why: The evaporative emissions system (charcoal canister and vent valves) clogs or fails, so air can't escape the tank while filling.
issues.next: Have the EVAP system tested. The canister, vent valve or filler neck may need replacement.

issues.t: Power windows stop working
issues.sym: A window won't go up or down, or works only sometimes.
issues.why: Window motors and wiring fail, and some owners report repeat failures.
issues.next: Have the window motor and switch checked. Close the window first if possible to keep weather out.

issues.t: Harsh or erratic automatic shifts
issues.sym: Rough, late or jerky automatic shifts.
issues.why: Hyundai's guidance is to confirm the transmission computer has the latest software and that the correct transmission fluid is used, since the wrong fluid or old software hurts shift quality.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to check for transmission software updates before replacing the fluid with the correct type. Avoid shops that use universal fluid.

issues.t: Car pulls to one side after alignment
issues.sym: The car pulls to the right and wears tires unevenly even after alignments.
issues.why: Hyundai issued a service bulletin for camber adjusting bolts, since a normal alignment may not have enough adjustment.
issues.next: Ask the shop to install camber adjusting bolts before aligning the car.

issues.t: Moisture inside headlights and taillights
issues.sym: Fog or water droplets inside the headlight or taillight lenses.
issues.why: Owners report condensation getting into the lamp housings.
issues.next: Light fog that clears is normal for vented lamps; standing water means a seal or crack problem and the lamp should be resealed or replaced.

issues.t: Front seat belts twist and won't retract (recall)
issues.sym: The front seat belts twist, jam, or are hard to pull out or retract.
issues.why: The belt webbing can twist in the D-ring guides. Hyundai recalled the cars to add a stopper, though some owners say the fix didn't last.
issues.next: Confirm the recall was done. If the belts still bind, have the belt or guide replaced; don't ride with a belt that won't latch or retract.

issues.t: Fuel tank can crack from emissions system vacuum (recall)
issues.sym: A gasoline smell or fuel leaking under the car.
issues.why: Vacuum from the evaporative emissions system could crack the fuel tank, causing a leak and fire risk.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall. If you smell fuel, have it inspected before driving.

issues.t: Windshield wipers can stop working (recall)
issues.sym: The wipers stop working, often in bad weather.
issues.why: Contaminated contacts in the wiper motor circuit breaker could cut power to the wipers.
issues.next: Confirm with a dealer that the wiper motor recall was done.

issues.t: Automatic transmission slips from a leaking valve (recall)
issues.sym: Slipping, weak acceleration, or flaring revs between gears.
issues.why: Seals on the pressure control solenoid valve could leak, so the transmission clutches slip.
issues.next: Confirm with a dealer that the valve was replaced under the recall.

issues.t: Automatic transmission stuck in gear or flaring
issues.sym: The automatic stays in one gear until high revs, flares between 2nd and 3rd, won't downshift, or slips.
issues.why: Owners report internal wear and valve body problems; skipped fluid changes make it worse.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and condition and have codes read. A fluid service sometimes helps; a rebuild may be needed if it slips.

issues.t: Cracked exhaust manifold
issues.sym: Ticking from the engine, exhaust smell in or near the car, or a louder exhaust.
issues.why: The exhaust manifold can crack after repeated heating and cooling. One owner says the repair was covered by a recall.
issues.next: Have the exhaust checked; fumes near the engine can enter the cabin. Ask a dealer if any coverage applies.

issues.t: Headlight bulbs burn out often
issues.sym: Headlight bulbs fail every few weeks or months, sometimes alternating sides, or the low beams are dim.
issues.why: Owners suspect a wiring or connector problem; dealers often found no defect.
issues.next: Check the headlight connectors for heat damage and corrosion, and have charging voltage tested.

issues.t: Wheel bearing noise when turning
issues.sym: A rumble, grinding or vibration that changes when turning.
issues.why: Owners report worn, crumbling wheel bearings, sometimes from rust.
issues.next: Have the bearings checked; a failing bearing can overheat and let the wheel wobble.
